_note: 27 MVP criteria (MVP=TRUE, Entity=Question). default_answer and default_note are pre-filled starting points — the evaluator confirms or overrides them based on evidence.

criteria.title: Planet-centered approach
criteria.question: Were the needs of the planet and ecological limits taken into account when developing the idea and project?
answers: A digital pollution & responsibility awareness training was realised.
The client has mapped the potential negative impacts of his project.
The client has set a continuous improvement strategy to tackle the potential negative impacts.
criteria.default_note: Manual verification needed — requires knowledge of team training records, client impact mapping exercises, and improvement strategy documents

criteria.title: Experience design
criteria.question: Are design choices (focus on decorative assets, user-journey and user interactions) relevant to UX and benefit the comprehension of the content?
answers: Decorative elements provide value to the design or a better comprehension of the content.
Decorative elements do not create readability issues.
User interactions are easy to understand and not create usability issues.
default_answer: Decorative elements do not create readability issues.
criteria.default_note: Partially verifiable — readability can be checked via contrast and layout analysis; design value and interaction usability need human review

criteria.title: Tracking & Data Management
criteria.question: Is your product exempt of page tracking removed or limited to what is really necessary?
answers: There is no unused page tracking in my product.
There is no unconsented page tracking in my product, this means a presence of a functional cookie bar.
Page tracking is limited to what is really necessary.
Users are be able to stop unwanted website tracking, this means the cookie settings can be accessed from the website.
default_answer: There is no unused page tracking in my product.
There is no unconsented page tracking in my product, this means a presence of a functional cookie bar.
Page tracking is limited to what is really necessary.
Users are be able to stop unwanted website tracking, this means the cookie settings can be accessed from the website.
criteria.default_note: Verify via network inspection — detect tracking scripts (GA, GTM, Facebook, Hotjar, etc.), check for cookie consent banner, and verify cookie settings are accessible

criteria.title: Need for images
criteria.question: Are the images creating a plus-value on the website without creating legibility issues?
answers: Images are essential and informative.
Images do not impair legibility.
default_answer: Images do not impair legibility.
criteria.default_note: Partially verifiable — legibility can be checked via contrast/overlay analysis; whether images are essential and informative needs human review

criteria.title: Optimize images
criteria.question: Are the images displayed optimally, taking into account the different screen resolutions, recent technologies and the loading time?
answers: Images are work in all browser, providing alternatives (transcripts, other file formats) when not compatible.
Images are compressed and optimized using modern format such as .webp.
Images are self-hosted.
The most appropriate image size is loaded by default.
Graphics and maps can be enlarged at the user's request.
default_answer: Images are work in all browser, providing alternatives (transcripts, other file formats) when not compatible.
Images are compressed and optimized using modern format such as .webp.
Images are self-hosted.
The most appropriate image size is loaded by default.
Graphics and maps can be enlarged at the user's request.
criteria.default_note: Verify via DOM inspection — check for <picture> elements, srcset attributes, WebP/AVIF sources, self-hosted image domains, and responsive sizing

criteria.title: Lazy loading
criteria.question: Is lazy loading used to ensure that image assets are only loaded when they are needed?
criteria.default_note: Verify via DOM check — below-fold images should have loading="lazy" attribute

criteria.title: Access alternatives (images)
criteria.question: Have you provided text alternatives for your users to access an image?
criteria.default_note: Verify via DOM check — non-decorative tags should have meaningful alt attributes (not empty, not just filename)

criteria.title: Need for media
criteria.question: Are video and audio content displayed adapted to the user's needs?
answers: Media content are essential and informative.
Media content do not autoplay.
Media content have controls to paused and muted.
Media content do not impair legibility.
default_answer: Media content are essential and informative.
Media content do not autoplay.
Media content have controls to paused and muted.
Media content do not impair legibility.
criteria.default_note: Verify via DOM inspection — check <video>/<audio> for autoplay attribute, controls attribute, and overlay/layout impact. N/A if no media on site.

criteria.title: Media optimization
criteria.question: Is the correct method being used to play a video or sound?
answers: Media content are work in all browser, providing alternatives (transcripts, other file formats) when not compatible.
Media content are compressed and optimized using modern format such as .webm.
Media content are self-hosted.
Multiple sizes are available, the most appropriate size is loaded by default.
default_answer: Media content are work in all browser, providing alternatives (transcripts, other file formats) when not compatible.
Media content are compressed and optimized using modern format such as .webm.
Media content are self-hosted.
Multiple sizes are available, the most appropriate size is loaded by default.
criteria.default_note: Verify via DOM and network inspection — check <video>/<source> for .webm format, self-hosted URLs, and multiple source sizes. N/A if no media on site.

criteria.title: Loading facade
criteria.question: Is there a loading mechanism to ensure that video and sound assets are only loaded when they are needed, without pre-loading?
criteria.default_note: Verify via network tab — reload page without playing media; if youtube/vimeo/media requests appear before user interaction, there is no facade. N/A if no media on site.

criteria.title: Access alternatives (media)
criteria.question: Have you provided media alternatives for your users to access a media?
answers: Subtitles are available.
Awareness is raised when a less appropriate size is loaded.
Video and audio can be switched off and alternatively accessed through transcripts or sufficient text alternatives.
default_answer: Subtitles are available.
criteria.default_note: Partially verifiable — can check for <track> elements and .vtt files; transcript availability and size awareness need human review. N/A if no media on site.

criteria.title: Avoid overburdening
criteria.question: Animations are behaving in a way that:
answers: Allows users to read and navigate the website without legibility issues.
Allows browsers and devices to run without frame drops due to overloading.
Allows users to have a similar experience without information loss no matter the internet speed, device or browser they have.
default_answer: Allows browsers and devices to run without frame drops due to overloading.
criteria.default_note: Partially verifiable — can measure FPS and CSS animation count; legibility impact and cross-device parity need human review. N/A if no animations on site.

criteria.title: Testing and validation
criteria.question: Are user tests regularly used to validate the assumptions?
criteria.default_note: Manual verification needed — requires knowledge of the team's user testing practices, survey cadence, and validation workflow

criteria.title: Mobile-friendliness
criteria.question: Is the user's experience also guaranteed on mobile devices without any loss?
criteria.default_note: Verify via DOM and viewport check — confirm <meta name="viewport"> is present, CSS uses responsive breakpoints, and no horizontal overflow on small screens

criteria.title: Performance goals
criteria.question: Did you set up and monitored performance goals?
answers: A page budget methodology has been defined and is used.
CPU usage and overall performance such as FPS have been monitored during development phases.
The website has been developed with slow internet and older devices compatibility taken into account.
default_answer: The website has been developed with slow internet and older devices compatibility taken into account.
criteria.default_note: Partially verifiable — can measure page weight against budget thresholds and test with throttled connection; whether a formal page budget methodology exists and FPS was monitored during dev needs human review

criteria.title: Minify code
criteria.question: Did you minify your code?
answers: HTML
CSS
Javascript
Data files (e.g JSON or RSS)
default_answer: HTML
CSS
Javascript
Data files (e.g JSON or RSS)
criteria.default_note: Verify via response inspection — fetch HTML/CSS/JS resources and check whitespace ratio; minified files have minimal newlines and indentation

criteria.title: Accessibility compliance
criteria.question: What kind of accessibility test have you performed on your product?
answers: Online accessibility checker such as Lighthouse
WCAG or RGAA Audit
User usability test
default_answer: Online accessibility checker such as Lighthouse
criteria.default_note: Partially verifiable — can run automated Lighthouse accessibility check; whether a formal WCAG audit or user usability test was performed needs human review

criteria.title: Third-party implementation
criteria.question: Are third-party content placed behind a facade (click-to-load mechanism) feature?
criteria.default_note: Verify via network inspection — reload page and check if third-party embeds (YouTube, Vimeo, Maps, social widgets) load without user interaction; if they do, there is no facade

criteria.title: Self-hosting and dependencies
criteria.question: How many third-party dependencies could you technically self-host to limit dependencies?
criteria.default_note: Verify via network inspection — count third-party domains serving resources that could technically be self-hosted (fonts, analytics libraries, embeddable widgets); 0 is ideal, higher is worse

criteria.title: Technology choice
criteria.question: The technologies used are:
answers: Stable
Secure
Appropriate for the products functionalities.
Appropriate based on the allowed ressources (human, time, budget and knowledge) given to create the product.
The most efficient languages that checks all the answers above.
default_answer: Stable
Secure
criteria.default_note: Partially verifiable — can detect tech stack (framework, libraries, versions) and check for known vulnerabilities or deprecated versions; appropriateness for project scope and resource constraints needs human review

criteria.title: Native features in the browser
criteria.question: How many custom components could have been replaced with a native feature of the browser?
criteria.default_note: Partially verifiable — can detect custom date pickers, modals, accordions, tooltips that have native HTML equivalents (<dialog>, <details>, <datalist>, popover); 0 is ideal, higher is worse

criteria.title: Minimum sustainability requirements
criteria.question: Does your hosting service:
answers: has verifiable labels or certifications showing their commitment for sustainability.
is providing sustainability-related key metrics publicly.
criteria.default_note: Partially verifiable — can identify the hosting provider from server headers and check Green Web Foundation database; verifying specific labels/certifications and public metrics requires visiting the hosting provider's website

criteria.title: Hosting location
criteria.question: Is your hosting provider geolocated accordingly to your audience location?
criteria.default_note: Verify via server headers — check server IP geolocation against the target audience region (e.g., Swiss site should be hosted in Europe)

criteria.title: Browser & Server-side caching
criteria.question: Is your server configured to render cached version of your content?
answers: HTML for static page
JS & CSS
Images, Fonts
Document files such as JSON and PDFs
default_answer: HTML for static page
JS & CSS
Images, Fonts
Document files such as JSON and PDFs
criteria.default_note: Verify via response headers — check Cache-Control and Expires headers for each resource type (HTML, CSS/JS, images/fonts, JSON/PDF)

criteria.title: Server-side compression
criteria.question: Which percentage of your website bandwidth usage is compressed when travelling over the network?
criteria.default_note: Verify via network inspection — compare 'kB transferred' vs 'kB resources' to compute compression ratio: (100 - (transferred/resources * 100)); check Content-Encoding headers for gzip/brotli

criteria.title: Refresh frequency
criteria.question: Is the refresh frequency adapted and defined on visitors needs?
criteria.default_note: Verify via network inspection — check for polling requests, WebSocket connections, or auto-refresh meta tags; data should only be fetched on user action, not on a timer

criteria.title: Lowest requirements
criteria.question: Did you select an infrastructure meeting with minimal specifications business requirements in terms of performance and availability?
criteria.default_note: Partially verifiable — can check for CDN usage, multi-region headers, and over-provisioning signals; whether the infrastructure tier matches actual business needs requires human review
